short: The world's first operational stealth aircraft, designed to evade radar detection.
full:
The Lockheed F-117 Nighthawk was introduced in October 1983 as the first operational aircraft engineered entirely around stealth technology. Developed in high secrecy by the Skunk Works division, its unusual faceted shape was specifically calculated to scatter radar waves, while its engines were heavily shielded to reduce infrared signatures. It lacked radar itself and relied on inertial navigation and thermal imaging for targeting.

The Nighthawk debuted publicly during the 1989 invasion of Panama and achieved widespread fame during the 1991 Gulf War, where it flew unimpeded through heavily defended Iraqi airspace to strike high-value targets. Although officially retired from frontline service in 2008 following the introduction of newer stealth fighters, several airframes continue to fly for research and adversary training purposes.
